sentences.text: Lapampasaurus cholinoi is the only known species of an extinct hadrosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Allen Formation in Argentina's La Pampa Province. The genus name refers to the province, while the species name honors collector José Cholino.
The holotype specimen represents a young adult measuring 5 to 6 meters in total length, though adults may have grown several meters larger.
Distinctive anatomical features include openings on the front neck vertebrae, a convex upper shoulder blade with a sharp lateral edge, and foot digits that are longer than wide with grooves and pits.
Named and described in 2012 by Rodolfo Coria, Bernardo González Riga, and Silvio Casadío, the holotype was found in a coastal barrier dating to about 70 million years ago.

The fossil consists of a partial skeleton lacking a skull, with bones that are poor in quality, incomplete, and heavily weathered. It is now part of the Paleovertebrate collection at the Provincial Museum of Natural History of La Pampa.
Researchers interpret the elongated grooves on the sides of the neck vertebrae as pneumatic foramina located in a pleurocoel, a type of air sac cavity.

Lapampasaurus is classified within the family Hadrosauridae, suborder Neornithischia, and order Ornithischia. Placing this dinosaur in Hadrosauridae suggests the group appeared in South America earlier than previously thought.
No exact cladistic analysis has been performed on Lapampasaurus to date.
Lapampasaurus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
It is debated whether the cervical vertebrae features are unique to Euornithopoda or expected of a Theropod member.
